transcription.tex: \textbf{Choose the axis}\par About the \(x\)-axis: integrate \(\pi y^2\) with respect to \(x\).\par About the \(y\)-axis: integrate \(\pi x^2\) with respect to \(y\).
\textbf{Choose the method}\par Convert limits when using a parameter.\par Subtract inner volumes for hollow regions.\par Apply cubic scale factors to volumes in models.

slides.title: Volumes of Revolution with harder integration

transcription.tex: The region \(R\) is bounded by the curve with equation \(y=\sin 2x\), the \(x\)-axis and \(x=\frac{\pi }{2}\). Find the volume of the solid formed when region \(R\) is rotated through \(2\pi \) radians about the \(x\)-axis.
A thin disc has radius \(y\) and thickness \(dx\).\[dV=\pi y^2dx,\qquad V=\pi\int_a^b y^2dx\]

transcription.tex: 3 The diagram shows the finite region $R$, which is bounded by the curve $y=\ln x$, the line $x=3$ and the $x$-axis. The region $R$ is rotated through $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis. Use integration to find the exact volume of the solid generated. (7 marks)\par Problem-solving\par You will need to find the value of $a$.
The curve meets the axis at \(x=1\). Integrate by parts twice:\[V=\pi\int_1^3(\ln x)^2dx\]\[=\pi[x(\ln x)^2-2x\ln x+2x]_1^3\]\[=\pi(3(\ln3)^2-6\ln3+4)\]

transcription.tex: The diagram shows the region $R$, which is bounded by the curve with equation $y=\sin x$, $0\le x\le \pi $ and the line with equation $y=\frac1{\sqrt2}$.\par Region $R$ is rotated through $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=\frac1{\sqrt2}$.\par Show that the solid of revolution formed has area $\frac{\pi }2(\pi -3)$.

The question calls the result an area. The disc integral gives the volume of the solid.\par The radius is the distance above the rotation axis:\[V=\pi\int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}(\sin x-1/\sqrt2)^2dx\]\[=\pi[x-\sin2x/4+\sqrt2\cos x]_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}\]\[=\frac\pi2(\pi-3)\]

transcription.tex: \textbf{8(a)} By writing a suitable expansion for \(\sin5\theta\), or otherwise, show that\[\sin^5\theta=\frac1{16}(10\sin\theta-5\sin3\theta+\sin5\theta).\]\par The curve shown in the diagram has equation \(x=\sin^2 y\sqrt{\sin y}\).\par The finite region bounded by the curve, the \(y\)-axis and the line \(y=\dfrac\pi4\) is shown in the diagram.\par The region is rotated through \(2\pi\) radians about the \(y\)-axis to generate a solid of revolution.\par (b) Show that the volume of the solid generated is \(\dfrac\pi{15}\left(8+\dfrac{43\sqrt2}8\right)\).
Writing \(s=\sin\theta\), use \(\sin3\theta=3s-4s^3\) and \(\sin5\theta=5s-20s^3+16s^5\); eliminate \(s^3\) and rearrange.

transcription.tex: The diagram shows a model of a goldfish bowl. The cross-section of the model is described by the curve with parametric equations \par \(x=2\sin t, y=2\cos t+2\), \(\frac{\pi }{6}\le t\le \frac{11\pi }{6}\), where the units of \(x\) and \(y\) are in cm. The goldfish bowl is formed by rotating this curve about the \(y\)-axis to form a solid of revolution.\par (a) Find the volume of water required to fill the model to a height of 3cm.\par The real goldfish bowl has a maximum diameter of 48cm.\par (b) Find the volume of water required to fill the real goldfish bowl to the corresponding height.
The model maximum diameter is 4 cm; linear scale factor is 12.\[V_{\rm real}=12^3(9\pi)=15552\pi\approx48900\ \mathrm{cm}^3\]
